🍅 When to plant tomato in Nigeria

Also called Tòmátì (Yoruba) and Tumatur (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant tomato in Nigeria from March to April and September to November and harvest from June to July and January to April. Main crop: nursery September–October, transplant October–November, harvest January–April in the North. Rain-fed crop: March–April.

PlantMarch to April and September to November
HarvestJune to July and January to April
Grows inAll regions
TypeFruit vegetables
Local namesTòmátì · Tumatur

About tomato

In 2016 the pest Tuta absoluta, nicknamed 'tomato ebola', destroyed many tomato farms in Kaduna and Kano.

How to plant tomato well

Pack fruits in plastic crates, not raffia baskets, to reduce crushing on the road.

Main crop: nursery September–October, transplant October–November, harvest January–April in the North. Rain-fed crop: March–April.

Diseases and pests of tomato

  • Tuta absoluta (tomato leaf miner)Use pheromone traps, rotate crops, remove infested plants and use recommended insecticides.
  • Early & late blightStake plants, space them well and use recommended fungicides such as mancozeb.
  • Bacterial wiltRotate with cereals and avoid waterlogged soil.

Best states for tomato

Kano · Kaduna · Katsina · Plateau · Bauchi · Gombe · Jigawa · Sokoto · Benue · Oyo · Ogun

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant tomato in Nigeria?

Plant tomato in Nigeria from March to April and September to November and harvest from June to July and January to April. Main crop: nursery September–October, transplant October–November, harvest January–April in the North. Rain-fed crop: March–April.

What is tomato called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Tomato is called Tòmátì (Yoruba) and Tumatur (Hausa).

When is tomato harvested in Nigeria?

Tomato is usually harvested from June to July and January to April.

Which Nigerian states grow the most tomato?

Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Jigawa, Sokoto, Benue, Oyo and Ogun are among the best-known tomato states.

Can I grow tomato in my part of Nigeria?

Yes. Tomato grows in every region of Nigeria: North and South.

What diseases attack tomato and how do I prevent them?

Tuta absoluta (tomato leaf miner): Use pheromone traps, rotate crops, remove infested plants and use recommended insecticides. Early & late blight: Stake plants, space them well and use recommended fungicides such as mancozeb. Bacterial wilt: Rotate with cereals and avoid waterlogged soil.
